regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY looks like acceleration — until you note that IIP YoY slipped to 6.7% from 8.8% and core sector eased to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%. The PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led: manufacturing PMI fell to 52.8 while services rose to 54.5, meaning the goods economy is losing the baton just as the investment cycle claims to be picking it up. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is the one number that earns the capex story credibility — but watch whether IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY is pulling forward orders or reflecting genuine new capacity decisions.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY is above RBI's 4.0% target, but the decomposition is what matters: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile print rising for two consecutive months — is doing the heavy lifting, while core CPI at 3.9% YoY is sticky but not spiralling. The inversion: if fuel is the driver and Brent has been flat month-on-month at $104.72/bbl, the base effect alone will keep fuel inflation elevated through Q3. RBI has already revised its inflation forecast to 5.1% YoY from 4.6% — that is not a minor adjustment; it is an admission that the pause will extend longer than the market is pricing.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY is a 630-bps flow divergence that the CD ratio of 81.4% — at the 75th percentile of its 10-year range — only partially captures. The second-order effect: NBFC credit growth jumped to 14.9% YoY from 10.6%, signalling that wholesale funding pressure is migrating from banks to non-bank lenders who have thinner liquidity buffers. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% while the repo rate was being held, the RBI moved to macro-prudential tightening via risk weights — credit card YoY already slowing to 2.3% from 5.6% suggests that process may already be underway.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate calculus has shifted: with RBI's own inflation forecast now at 5.1% YoY, the ex-ante real repo rate is barely positive. That is not a cutting environment — it is a holding environment with a hawkish tilt that the market has not fully priced. For housing, the average home loan rate at 7.25% p.a. is at only the 25th percentile of its 10-year range, which is why home loan disbursements are running at ₹19,930 cr / quarter. The risk: if fuel inflation forces RBI to signal a hike rather than a cut, mortgage repricing would arrive precisely as unsold inventory is rising.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — up from 75.6% prior month — make the capex upcycle the most credible regime signal in today's data. Credit to industry at 20.0% YoY and credit to services at 22.9% YoY confirm that financing is flowing, not just being announced. The inversion: core sector at 5.4% YoY and falling is the leading edge of capex output, and it is decelerating. If order books are robust but core sector is softening, either the orders are being deferred or the capacity additions are not yet translating into throughput — watch cement and steel dispatch for the ground truth.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month is a strong number — but a 14.6% jump from ₹1,74,116 cr / month prior deserves scrutiny: how much is genuine demand versus year-end advance filings and formalisation reclassification? Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY are the proxies that validate the GST print — both are at or above the 50th percentile, suggesting the consumption signal is real. The divergence to watch: e-commerce GMV growth at 18% YoY is at only the 26th percentile, implying that the consumption strength is concentrated in physical durables and vehicles rather than broad-based digital spend — urban affluent, not mass market.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (latest, down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile of 10-year range. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months: 82.5% → 81.4% masks the underlying flow stress — credit is still outpacing deposits by 630 bps. NBFC credit growth at 14.9% YoY (latest, up from 10.6% prior) signals wholesale funding pressure is shifting to non-bank lenders.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% and deposit franchises in metros (HDFC Bank, Kotak, ICICI). Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities — they face margin compression as deposit costs rise. RBI will likely signal rate cuts in Q2 FY27 to ease deposit pressure, but near-term funding stress will persist. Hedge via short duration fixed income.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically precedes either RBI rate cuts or a sharp tightening in credit growth. The last time CD ratio was this elevated (2022), credit growth decelerated 400 bps within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (latest, up from 75.6% prior month) — now at 74th percentile of 10-year range — indicates headroom for capex without overcapacity risk. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (latest, down from 6.0% prior) is moderating but remains positive. Credit to industry at 20.0% YoY (latest, up from 6.5% prior) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (latest, up from 10.2% prior) confirm capex financing is flowing. Order books remain robust across auto, infra, and manufacturing.","implication":"Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Timken, Xylem), infra equipment (Voltas, Thermax), and cement (UltraTech, Ambuja). Capex cycle typically runs 18–24 months; we are in month 8–10 of this upcycle. Allocate to PSU capex plays (NTPC, Power Grid, ONGC) as government spending accelerates into FY27. Avoid consumer discretionary — capex is crowding out consumption.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at the 74th percentile; historically, sustained capex cycles begin when CU crosses 75% and credit to industry accelerates above 15% YoY. Both conditions are met.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Affluent Money Entering Via SIP Backdoor","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,297 ₹ cr / month (latest, up from 31,961 ₹ cr / month prior month) — rising 2 consecutive months and at 92nd percentile of 10-year range. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (latest, up from 99.06 mn prior month) at 82nd percentile. But SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (latest, up from 18.21 ₹ lakh cr prior month) is at 93rd percentile — growing faster than account growth. This implies average ticket size per SIP account is rising: 18.62 lakh cr ÷ 100.18 mn accounts = ₹1.86 lakh per account, up from ₹1.84 lakh prior month. MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (latest, up from 85.76 ₹ lakh cr prior month) at 86th percentile. DII equity net at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 35,099 ₹ cr net / month prior month) — at 100th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months.","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour. Affluent retail (HNI/UHNI) are entering via SIP to appear disciplined while deploying large sums. Overweight large-cap quality (Nifty 50 constituents with ROE > 18%) and avoid small/mid-cap momentum plays. Expect SIP growth to decelerate once market corrects 8–12%; use that as a rebalancing opportunity. DII strength masks FII weakness (FII net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month, up from -3,111.9 ₹ cr net / month prior month, but still volatile). Domestic flows are masking foreign selling.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile preceded market corrections in 2018 and 2022 by 4–6 months. Rising average ticket size is a classic late-cycle signal — mass retail enters early, affluent enters late.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Credibility","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, up from 20.05% YoY prior month) — at 95th percentile of 10-year range and rising 2 consecutive months. Brent crude at 104.72 $/bbl (latest, flat from prior month) but up 4 of last 5 months from 100.5 $/bbl. WTI at 91.85 $/bbl (latest, flat from prior month) but up 3 of last 5 months from 89.48 $/bbl. Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY (latest, up from 4.38% YoY prior month) — now above RBI's 4.0% comfort zone. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY (latest) remains sticky. RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (latest, up from 4.6% YoY prior month) signals RBI expects further overshoot.","implication":"RBI will NOT cut rates in Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27 despite deposit stress. This creates a policy bind: credit growth will remain elevated (17.1% YoY) while rates stay at 5.25% p.a., forcing NBFCs to compete harder for deposits. Hedge via long-duration fixed income (10-year GSec yields at 5.22% yield, down from 5.28% yield prior month, at 95th percentile — yields are near cycle lows). Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) as oil prices hold above $100/bbl. Avoid consumer staples with high fuel pass-through (FMCG, logistics).","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a 10-year high. The last time fuel inflation exceeded 20% YoY (2022), RBI held rates steady for 6 months despite growth concerns, leading to a 200 bps rally in 10-year yields.","is_surprise":false}

(latest, up from 0.75% p.a. prior month) — at 86th percentile of 10-year range and rising. Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (latest, up from 3.63% p.a. prior month) — at 68th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (latest, up from 2.0% p.a. prior month) — at 59th percentile. US 10-year Treasury at 5.22% yield (latest, down from 5.28% yield prior month) — at 95th percentile, near cycle lows. DXY at 102.231 index (latest, flat from prior month) — at 56th percentile, stable. US PMI composite at 56 index (latest, up from 54.5 index prior month) — at 84th percentile, strong. China PMI composite at 49.5 index (latest, up from 49.3 index prior month) — at 47th percentile, below 50 (contraction).","implication":"BOJ tightening is gradual but real; carry trades funded in JPY are unwinding slowly. This divergence will keep USD bid and EM currencies under pressure. Reduce INR exposure; hedge via USD forwards or long DXY positions. Avoid EM debt; prefer US Treasuries (5.22% yield is attractive on a 2-year horizon).","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"BOJ at 86th percentile signals policy normalization is accelerating. The last time BOJ was this hawkish (2018), carry trades unwound sharply, causing a 3–4% INR depreciation within 3 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Signals RBI Intervention Limits","data_text":"INR/USD at 97.09 ₹ (latest, up from 96.73 ₹ prior month) — at 94th percentile of 10-year range, near 10-year highs. INR has depreciated 4 of last 5 months from 95.24 ₹. FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from -3,111.9 ₹ cr net / month prior month) — volatile, at 83rd percentile. But FII flows are lumpy; the prior month was -3,111.9 ₹ cr net / month (outflow). This suggests FII are rotating, not committing. DII equity net at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 35,099 ₹ cr net / month prior month) — at 100th percentile, domestic flows are masking foreign selling. Brent crude at 104.72 $/bbl (latest) keeps India's import bill elevated; CAD pressure is building.","implication":"RBI is likely intervening to defend INR but reserves are finite. If INR breaks 97.50 ₹/USD, expect RBI to signal a more hawkish stance (rate hold or hike) to attract FII. This would conflict with deposit stress (CD ratio at 81.4%) and capex financing needs. Hedge via long USD positions or INR put options (97.50 strike). Avoid rupee-denominated debt; prefer USD-linked returns. Overweight exporters (IT, pharma, auto) who benefit from INR weakness; underweight importers (oil, metals, electronics).","pct_10y":94,"pct_note":"INR at 94th percentile is a 10-year high. The last time INR was this weak (2022), RBI raised rates 190 bps over 6 months to defend the currency, causing a sharp equity correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pivot Away","data_text":"Office absorption at 3.4 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, down from 3.5 mn sq ft / quarter prior month) — at 0th percentile of 10-year range (lowest on record). But office vacancy at 9.6% vacant (latest, down from 11.2% vacant prior month) — at 16th percentile, improving. This paradox reveals the truth: existing office stock is being absorbed by Global Capability Centers (GCCs) and non-IT tenants, NOT traditional IT services firms. Nifty IT index is flat (recent: 22,422 → 22,556 → 22,776 → 22,603 → 22,232 → 22,520 index, up 3 of last 5 months) while office vacancy is collapsing. Retail mall vacancy at 5.0% vacant (latest, down from 5.6% vacant prior month) — at 8th percentile, tightest in 10 years. Retail absorption is STRONG (84th percentile signal score) while office absorption is WEAK (-100 signal score). This divergence is the tell: consumer spending is robust (GST at 199,853 ₹ cr / month, up from 174,116 ₹ cr / month prior month, at 71st percentile), but IT services capex is stalling. GCCs are consolidating into fewer, larger hubs (Bangalore, Hyderabad) and moving away from traditional office parks.","implication":"SELL Nifty IT on any rally above 22,800 index. The office absorption collapse is a leading indicator of IT services margin compression — GCCs are negotiating lower rents and consolidating headcount. Overweight commercial real estate plays with GCC exposure (Embassy Office Parks, Mindspace REIT) but ONLY if they can pivot to non-IT tenants (e.g., fintech, healthcare, manufacturing). Retail mall plays (Indiabulls Real Estate, Phoenix Mills) are the true beneficiary of the consumption surge; they are decoupling from office RE. The market is pricing IT as a growth story; it is now a value trap. Retail RE is the hidden capex beneficiary.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile (lowest on record) while retail mall vacancy at 8th percentile (tightest on record) is a 10-year divergence. This has never happened before — it signals a structural shift in real estate demand away from IT services toward consumer-facing businesses.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carrying Growth While Goods Economy Quietly Fades

The facts:

  • PMI Composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) — but Manufacturing PMI fell to 52.8 while Services PMI rose to 54.5; the goods economy is losing momentum.
  • IIP YoY slipped to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%; Core Sector eased to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% — both decelerating even as the capex narrative strengthens.
  • Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6%) is the one number that earns the investment cycle credibility.
  • But GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month — a ₹25,737 cr jump from prior month — warrants decomposition: advance filings and formalisation effects cannot be ruled out.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY and PMI at 54.6 signal expansion; IIP and core sector are both decelerating. Services are masking goods-economy softness that the investment cycle has not yet reversed.

Bottom line: Watch IIP capital goods in the next print — a second consecutive deceleration would signal the capex upcycle is order-book deep but not yet output-wide.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

Copper Prices a Recovery That China's PMI Refuses to Confirm

The facts:

  • Copper at $6.69/lb (80th percentile, up 3 of last 5 sessions) is pricing a global industrial upcycle.
  • But China PMI Composite at 49.5 (47th percentile, below 50) signals contraction; China GDP slowed to 4.3% YoY from 5.0%.
  • US PMI Composite at 56 (84th percentile) and US GDP SAAR rising to 2.2% SAAR from 1.5% provide the DM counterweight.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.22% yield (95th percentile) — even after slipping from 5.28% — keeps real tightening embedded in the curve regardless of Fed pause.

The tension: Copper and US PMI are pricing synchronised global recovery; China's contraction-zone PMI and decelerating GDP mean the commodity signal is a DM story, not a global one — and DM growth at 5.22% real rates has a shelf life.

Bottom line: Avoid commodity-linked EM plays premised on China reflation; the copper move is a US-capex signal, not a China-demand signal.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows at Record Highs — But Funded by Deposits That Aren't Growing

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile, rising 2 consecutive months); SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile) — average ticket per account rising to ₹1.86 lakh.
  • DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months) — absorbing FII volatility.
  • But bank deposit growth at 10.8% YoY against credit growth of 17.1% YoY — a 630-bps flow divergence — means the savings pool funding SIPs is not growing fast enough to also fund bank lending.
  • NBFC credit growth jumped to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% — wholesale funding stress migrating to thinner-buffered non-bank lenders.

The tension: Equity liquidity is at record strength; banking system liquidity is structurally strained. The same household that is increasing SIP ticket size is not growing their bank deposit at the same pace — capital is rotating from deposits to MFs, tightening bank funding.

Bottom line: Watch RBI's next macro-prudential signal — a risk-weight circular on NBFC lending would be the trigger for a liquidity repricing across the credit stack.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand and GCC Consolidation Rewriting the Real Estate Map

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 5 pp from 15% prior); NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $140 bn (12.8% YoY).
  • Premium (₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr) commands 34% of launch supply — the largest band — while affordable (<₹40 lakh) at 14% launch share is outselling its supply at 16% demand share.
  • Office absorption at 3.4 mn sq ft / quarter (0th percentile — lowest on record) masks a GCC-led vacancy compression: office vacancy fell to 9.6% vacant from 11.2%; GCCs now 41% of occupier mix vs IT services at 15%.
  • But office REITs are pricing the old IT-services narrative: Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit (down from ₹431), Mindspace at ₹345/unit (down from ₹494) — the market has not yet priced the GCC upgrade.

The tension: Residential demand is NRI- and premium-led with genuine absorption; office absorption is at a record low by volume but vacancy is tightening — the GCC consolidation into fewer, larger hubs (Hyderabad at 5.3 mn sq ft / quarter, Bengaluru at 4.9 mn sq ft / quarter) is invisible in the aggregate number.

Bottom line: Office REIT valuations pricing IT-services stagnation are mispricing the GCC upgrade cycle — Hyderabad and Bengaluru-focused exposure is the asymmetric trade.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Pressure Points — One Catalyst Away From Compounding

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months) with Brent flat at $104.72/bbl — any supply shock adds directly to CPI and forces RBI's hand.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY — a macro-prudential tightening circular is the non-linear risk.
  • INR at 97.09 ₹ (94th percentile, depreciated 4 of last 5 months from 95.24 ₹) — Brent at $104.72/bbl keeps CAD pressure building; FII flows at ₹29,631 cr net / month are lumpy and reversible.
  • BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) — yen carry unwind is slow but directional; US 10Y at 5.22% yield (95th percentile) keeps the pressure on EM capital flows.

The tension: Each risk is manageable in isolation; the compounding scenario is Brent staying above $100/bbl forcing RBI to hold or hike, which widens the real rate gap, attracts carry but pressures INR on CAD, while BOJ tightening simultaneously unwinds the yen carry that has been funding EM inflows.

Bottom line: Watch RBI's inflation forecast revision at the next MPC meeting — any upward move above 5.1% YoY closes the door on rate cuts and opens the door on macro-prudential tightening.

"}
